The engineering study a utility runs before connecting a large new load or generator: what the request does to the network, which transformers, lines and substations it overloads, and what upgrades are needed. It follows a feasibility screen and precedes a facilities study that prices those upgrades — and each study is valid only against the grid as modelled that day, which is why the date moves.

The company that assembles cells, enclosures, cooling, power conversion and control software into a complete storage product and warrants it as one system. The buyer's warranty and service relationship is with the integrator, not the cell maker, which is why an integrator's failure strands support even when the cells are healthy.

A Texas mechanism from a 2023 statute under which a wires utility files a multi-year plan of hardening, wildfire-mitigation, flood and cyber investments for commission approval, then recovers the approved cost through a rider. It moves a class of spending out of the contested rate case and into a pre-approved program.

How firmly a point on the network holds its voltage, and how much fault current it can supply. Strong points tolerate large converters; weak ones make them unstable — and a large new plant or load can itself weaken the point it connects to.

The slow decay of current in an IGBT after its gate has been turned off, caused by charge stored in the device that has nowhere to go. It happens at full bus voltage, so it is a direct energy loss on every switching cycle and is the main reason IGBTs are run at low switching frequencies.

A contract in which the buyer pays for a committed quantity whether or not it is used. It shifts utilization risk to the buyer and turns a speculative revenue line into one lenders will underwrite — the structure behind both colocation leases and the minimum-take terms in large-load utility tariffs.
A transaction in which investors buy all the shares of a listed company and delist it. The company stops publishing quarterly results and answers to its new owners instead of to a share price.

A plug-in unit that clamps onto an energised busway to take a circuit off it, usually carrying its own breaker or fuses. It is what makes busway reconfigurable, and it is also the point where a new load can be added without anyone re-checking the protection upstream.

The moment a chip design is finished and sent to the foundry to be made. It is the point of no return in a silicon schedule: after it, fixing a design error means another pass costing months and a great deal of money.

The ability, created by the 2022 US climate law, to sell clean-energy tax credits for cash to an unrelated party rather than monetizing them through a tax-equity partnership. It turns credits into a near-cash financing source for utilities with limited tax appetite, usually at a discount to face value that the seller must account for.

Capital from an investor — usually a bank — that owns part of a project so it can use the project's federal tax credits and depreciation against its own tax bill. The project gets cash up front; the investor gets tax benefits it could not otherwise use.

A short loan that advances the money a tax-equity investor or credit buyer will pay at commercial operation, so the project can be built first. It is repaid the day the tax equity or credit-transfer proceeds arrive.

Transmission cost of service: the revenue requirement a transmission owner is allowed to collect for its wires, set by the commission and, in ERCOT, recovered from every distribution utility on a postage-stamp basis through a wholesale transmission rate. It can be updated between full rate cases as new lines enter service, so a wires utility's transmission build shows up on bills within months.

Transmission and distribution utility: in a restructured market such as Texas, the regulated company that owns only the wires — poles, lines, substations, meters — and earns its return on that rate base. It owns no generation and sells no energy; retail providers buy delivery from it, and the commission sets its rates. Oncor, CenterPoint and AEP Texas are the pattern.

The review lenders commission before financing a project, covering the equipment, its certifications and test evidence, the supplier's track record and finances, the contracts and the policy exposure. It asks what happens if things go wrong and who pays, rather than how good the technology is.

A standards body's interim document — prepared by a task group rather than approved by a full technical committee — published quickly to fill a gap until a consensus standard exists. CSA TS-800:24 was one; CSA C800:25 is the consensus standard that replaced it.

An older land-use category, written for switching and carrier buildings, under which some cities still classify data centers. Where it survives, a campus can be approved by staff or a planning commission without the council vote a new category would require.

The temperature difference a refrigeration machine has to pump heat across — condensing temperature minus evaporating temperature. Compressor work rises with lift, so every degree given back at either end is money.

The share of a landlord's rent that comes from one or a few tenants. High concentration lowers the cost of debt while the tenant is strong and makes the landlord's fortunes track that tenant's capital spending.

The entity whose name is on a data-center lease and who owes the rent — not necessarily the company whose computers fill the building. In the AI buildout an intermediary can be tenant of record for a frontier lab that never signs the lease.

The twelve-month period of actual costs and sales a rate case uses as its base. A historic test year uses costs already incurred; a forecast or future test year projects them forward. The choice matters: a utility investing faster than it depreciates recovers less under a historic year, which is why commissions sometimes impose one as a discipline.

The industry of independent laboratories and certifiers — UL Solutions, Intertek, SGS, Bureau Veritas, TÜV, DEKRA, CSA Group's commercial arm — that tests products, inspects installations and issues the certificates and marks that markets and regulators accept.

A thin ceramic layer sprayed onto turbine blades and combustor walls so the metal underneath runs a couple of hundred degrees cooler than the gas around it. It is what allows firing temperatures well above the melting point of the alloy, and its condition is a large part of what an overhaul inspects.

The heat a processor is designed to give off at sustained load, in watts — the number a cold plate and the coolant flow behind it are sized to remove. AI accelerators went from about 700 W to 1,400 W in two generations and are heading past 2,000 W, which is what drives rack power and CDU capacity.

Storing cooling rather than electricity: chilled water or ice made when power is cheap or plentiful and drawn on later. In a critical facility it is also the ride-through that covers a chiller restart.

Nitrogen oxide formed when the nitrogen already in combustion air reacts with oxygen in a hot flame — the dominant source for gas-fired plant. Its rate climbs exponentially with temperature, so hot streaks matter more than the average, and every mainstream control works by making the flame cooler or more uniform.

How hard it is for heat to escape from a part to the air or liquid that carries it away, measured as temperature rise per watt. A converter's current rating is really a thermal statement: the current it can carry before its junction temperature reaches the limit through the path it has been given.

A self-accelerating overheating reaction inside a battery cell: heat triggers reactions that release more heat, potentially propagating cell to cell. The failure mode BESS safety standards are designed to contain.
A reactor whose neutrons have been slowed by a moderator to roughly the thermal energy of their surroundings. Almost every operating commercial reactor is one.

An inverter whose output can sit at three voltage steps rather than two, usually by clamping to the midpoint of a split DC link. Each switch then blocks half the voltage and the output waveform starts closer to a sine wave, so both switching losses and the output filter shrink — the main reason large modern UPS units reach efficiencies in the high nineties where two-level designs did not.

The strictest US EPA emission stage for diesel engines, cutting nitrogen oxides and particulates to a small fraction of earlier stages, usually with after-treatment such as SCR and a particulate filter. Emergency-only stationary engines are held to an earlier stage; a diesel that will run for prime power, peak shaving or demand response generally must meet it — the regulatory fork in a data center's generator strategy.
Casting a building's wall panels flat on the slab and then craning them upright into place. Fast, cheap and weather-tolerant, which is why so many large single-storey buildings are built this way.

A plot of how long a protective device takes to operate against how much current it sees, drawn on log-log paper so a whole series of devices can be compared on one sheet. Nesting the curves so the downstream device always clears first is what selective coordination means in practice; where two curves cross or touch, selectivity is lost at that current.

The months between a generating unit landing on site and its first delivered watt. The number a generation-first developer sequences its fleet by: mobile aeroderivatives in about two months, refurbished small frames in eight, new industrial frames in fifteen, heavy F-class units in about twenty-two.
A storage contract where the offtaker pays a fixed fee for the right to charge and discharge the battery as they wish — the owner operates the asset, the toller takes the market risk.
The traditional cooling unit: the rate of heat removal that would freeze one short ton of ice in a day, about 3.517 kW. A megawatt of IT load needs roughly 284 tons of cooling.

The moulds, jigs, fixtures and test rigs made specifically to build one product. Who paid for it and who is named as its owner in the contract is often the single fact that decides how quickly production can be moved somewhere else.

A package that takes heat out through its upper face into a heatsink or cold plate instead of down into the board. It matters when the underside of the board is full or the board itself is a poor thermal path — increasingly the case as converters move under the processor.

A headline number that may include optional renewal periods, pass-through costs or capacity not yet built. Because there is no accounting definition, two companies can quote very different figures for economically similar deals.

The whole cost of running something over its life — purchase price plus power, cooling, space, maintenance and the staff to operate it — rather than the price on the invoice. In a data centre the electricity and cooling over a few years commonly exceed what the hardware cost.

Everything a campus draws for a tenant — the IT load plus cooling, distribution losses and building services. A rent quoted on total facility power must be divided by the PUE to compare with a rent quoted on critical IT load.

The declared replacement cost of everything a property policy covers at a location, plus the business income at risk. It is the denominator behind a rate, so an understated figure quietly turns a good-looking rate into an inadequate limit.

Recordable injuries multiplied by two hundred thousand and divided by hours worked — the constant being one hundred workers at forty hours for fifty weeks, so the result reads as recordables per hundred workers per year. The arithmetic is unstable at small scale: on a small firm's hours a single incident moves the rate by a whole point, which is why the same threshold means very different things for a large contractor and a small one.

Tensor Processing Unit: Google's own AI accelerator chip, designed in-house and built with Broadcom, used inside Google Cloud and now sold or leased to outside buyers as an alternative to NVIDIA GPUs.

The ability to reconstruct any delivered unit's history — which components it contains, when and where they were made, what the process readings were, and where it shipped. It converts an unbounded quality problem into a bounded one, and because the links are destroyed at assembly unless captured then, it is a production-line design decision rather than a report.

Putting more crews into a work area than it can hold, so that they queue for access, work around each other's unfinished work and interfere with one another. It is the usual reason adding people to a late project produces less extra output than expected, and it raises safety exposure at the same time as it cuts productivity.
Amazon's own AI training and inference chip, built for AWS and offered to customers as a lower-cost alternative to NVIDIA GPUs. Anthropic is its anchor user.

The most power a corridor can actually carry, set by whichever constraint binds first — conductor heating, voltage collapse, or the stability of the machines at each end. It usually sits well below the sum of the lines' thermal ratings.

The interval between the normal supply failing and the load being carried by the alternate source — sensing, engine start and stabilization, then the switch itself. Stored energy must cover all of it; the standards fix the outer bound and the design decides how much shorter it actually is.

A device that changes AC voltage through two magnetically coupled windings, stepping transmission voltage down through substation, medium-voltage, and unit tiers until equipment can use it. Every step costs a little efficiency, a data-center power chain passes through several, and the lead time on large units is one of the buildout's hardest constraints.

A UPS built without the bulky low-frequency transformer that older designs used to derive the output neutral and provide isolation, using higher-frequency switching and a split DC link instead. It is markedly smaller, lighter and more efficient — and it hands the neutral and fault-current questions the transformer used to answer back to the system designer.

A contract between a utility and a very large new customer, filed with the federal regulator, under which the customer posts security for the transmission upgrades it triggers and commits to take the capacity. The federal half of connecting a gigawatt campus; the state half is the retail service agreement.

A listed company whose main purpose is to hold a digital asset on its balance sheet so that its shares act as a proxy for that asset. It raises equity or debt to buy more, and trades at a premium or discount to what it holds.

Reinsurance bought for a whole book of business at once: every policy meeting the treaty's definition is automatically covered for its term, with no individual underwriting. It is how a carrier buys capacity in bulk, usually renewed annually on 1 January, 1 April or 1 July.
A lease in which the tenant pays rent plus property taxes, insurance and maintenance — the landlord collects a clean number and the tenant carries the operating-cost risk. Written NNN.

Tri-structural isotropic fuel: a sub-millimetre uranium kernel wrapped in layers of carbon and silicon carbide that hold fission products inside the particle even at very high temperatures — the fuel form that lets a gas reactor claim its containment is in the fuel itself.

Air bled from the compressor and piped through hollow blades and vanes so they survive gas hotter than their own melting point. It is a direct loss — that air was compressed at cost and does no work in the combustor — so every design is a trade between how hot the machine can fire and how much of its own air it must spend to allow it.

The delay between asking a turbocharged engine for more power and the turbocharger spooling up enough air to burn the extra fuel. It is the physical reason a large diesel cannot always take its full rating in one step, and the reason load-acceptance figures are quoted per step with a recovery time.

Using exhaust energy to spin a turbine that drives a compressor, forcing more air — and so more fuel — into the same cylinder. It is what recovers the output a lean-burn engine gives away by burning with excess air, and it is why a modern gas engine reaches efficiencies comparable to a much larger turbine.

A manufacturing contract in which the builder buys all the materials as well as doing the work, and sells a finished unit at one price. It hands the builder the purchasing margin and the inventory risk together — the opposite of a consignment deal.

A contract under which one engineering, procurement and construction firm delivers the whole plant ready to operate, so the buyer need not manage suppliers. Available Power attached Linxon to projects it sold so a financial buyer could own without building.

A diode rectifier fed through two transformer windings phase-shifted by thirty degrees, so the two halves' distortion partly cancels and the current drawn is much closer to a sine wave than a plain six-pulse bridge manages. It was the standard way to make a large UPS or drive tolerable to its upstream supply before active front ends took over.

A national regime in which an authority approves a product type for sale or use in that market, commonly recognising international test standards and sometimes adding local testing. Where a foreign test report is not recognised, the testing is simply repeated — which is a large part of why compliance work does not travel.

The American safety and listing standard for inverters and converters interconnecting with the grid. It is the test-and-listing document rather than the requirement: IEEE 1547 says what a resource must do, and a UL 1741 listing demonstrates that a given product does it.

The supplement certifying the smart-inverter grid-support functions required by California Rule 21's first phase — voltage and frequency ride-through, power-factor control and volt-var among them — using test methods it defined itself rather than the IEEE conformance procedures.

The supplement certifying compliance with IEEE 1547-2018, using the IEEE 1547.1-2020 conformance test procedures rather than its own. The practical difference from SA is that the laboratory now runs exactly the tests the interconnection standard specifies, so listing and requirement line up.

The North American safety standard for stationary batteries — construction, protection and abuse testing for a battery meant to live in a building or a container. Listing to it is usually the first thing a fire marshal asks for.

The North American safety standard and system-level listing for a complete energy storage system — battery, conversion, controls and enclosure evaluated as one assembly. It is the certification that produces permission to install, as distinct from the test method that produces fire and propagation data.
The test method that characterizes how battery fires start and propagate at cell, module, unit, and installation level. Its data feeds fire-safety design and permitting for storage projects.

The sequence of abuse tests — altitude, thermal cycling, vibration, shock, short circuit, impact, overcharge and forced discharge — that a lithium battery design must pass before it may legally be transported. It is a shipping qualification and says nothing about whether the product may be installed.

The insurance market's swing between hard and soft conditions. Losses erode capital, capacity withdraws, prices rise, high prices attract new capital, capacity returns and prices fall again. Almost every broker revenue trend is partly this cycle rather than the broker.

A generator's capacity discounted for how often it is expected to be unavailable, so that a megawatt of one resource can be compared with a megawatt of another. Capacity markets buy and pay for unforced capacity, not nameplate.
The distributed weight per unit area a floor is rated to carry, in pounds per square foot. Data halls are rated far above office space, and liquid-cooled rows above conventional halls.

A switch that conducts with one kind of charge carrier only, like a MOSFET. It has no stored charge to clear when it turns off, so it switches quickly and cleanly, but its resistance climbs steeply with voltage rating.

The tiers of ownership units in an LLC or partnership — 'A units' and 'B units' — whose rights to cash, control and returns are set by the operating agreement rather than by how many units each party holds. The class terms, not the chart, say who gets the money.

The hours needed to install one of something — one pile, one tracker row, one termination, one metre of cable. Multiplied by quantity it is the labour estimate and divided into the schedule it is the crew plan, so a fixed-price bid is fundamentally a bet that these numbers are right.
The quarterly narrative a listed partnership or company sends its owners alongside the numbers. For a private subsidiary it is often the only place the sponsor states what it paid and what it bought.

A listing structure in which the public company owns units of an underlying operating partnership or LLC; pre-IPO owners keep their partnership units and matching high-vote shares, so control and tax treatment differ from an ordinary IPO.

A structure in which a REIT holds its properties through an operating partnership rather than directly. Sellers can take partnership units instead of cash and defer tax, which is why large property deals are often paid for partly in units.

Uninterruptible power supply: a power stage backed by stored energy — a battery string or a spinning flywheel — that carries the load through grid disturbances until generators start. In data centers it sits between utility power and the IT load.

The cabinet a modular UPS's power modules plug into — internal busbars, input and output breakers, controls, and empty slots. Buying the frame fixes the maximum capacity; populating it decides today's.

A self-contained UPS building block: rectifier, inverter, control and cooling in one chassis that slides into a shared frame and shares the load with its neighbours. Capacity is bought a module at a time, and a failed one is exchanged while the rest keep carrying the load.

The Uptime Institute's availability ladder for data centers: Tier I basic, Tier II redundant components, Tier III concurrently maintainable — any part serviceable without downtime — and Tier IV fault-tolerant, surviving any single failure. It is the shorthand buyers use for how much redundancy, and how much capital, a facility carries.

The accounting rulebook used by companies reporting to the US Securities and Exchange Commission as domestic filers. It is generally more prescriptive than IFRS and more reluctant to revalue assets upward.

A medium-voltage breaker whose contacts part inside a sealed vacuum bottle. With almost nothing to ionise, the arc dies at the first current zero and the gap recovers its strength in microseconds — which is why vacuum displaced oil and gas interruption at distribution voltages and why the bottle, not the mechanism, is the part that defines the breaker's life.

The four-step loop every chiller, refrigerator and air conditioner runs on: a liquid evaporates and absorbs heat, a compressor raises its pressure and temperature, it condenses and gives the heat up somewhere hotter, and an expansion device drops it back down.

An accounting label for a company that another company controls and must consolidate into its own accounts even without owning it outright. Seeing a subsidiary described this way tells you the parent reports its results as its own.
A plant with one variable-flow pumping loop that runs through the chillers themselves, saving pumping energy at the cost of having to respect each machine's minimum flow.

The Virginia Clean Economy Act of 2020: the state law that sets Dominion Energy Virginia on a path to carbon-free generation by 2045 and mandates specific gigawatts of solar, offshore wind and energy storage along the way, executed through annual filings the commission approves. It is the statutory reason the utility runs a standing storage procurement.
Virtual design and construction: building the building once in a coordinated 3-D model so that clashes between structure, ductwork, pipe and conduit are found on a screen rather than in the field.

Owning more than one consecutive step of a supply chain — designing, building and servicing the same product, for instance. It shortens hand-offs and captures more margin, at the cost of concentrating risk and reducing the buyer's ability to compare.

Mounting the final converters directly beneath the processor package, on the far side of the board, so current flows straight up through the board into the chip instead of sideways across it. The shorter path cuts resistive loss and frees the board area around the package for signal connections.

A utility that owns generation, transmission and distribution and sells to the end customer under one regulated franchise — Dominion Energy Virginia, Georgia Power and Entergy are the pattern. Contrast a wires-only utility in a restructured market such as Texas, which delivers power it does not generate. Which kind sits across the table decides whether the utility buys plants or only substations.
The year a fund makes its first investment, used to compare funds that faced the same market conditions.

Delivering gas by road as compressed or liquefied fuel when no adequate pipe reaches a site. It genuinely works and is how some on-site plants start, but it means a storage yard, regasification or decompression equipment, continuous truck movements, and a delivered fuel cost well above pipeline gas.

A fleet of small, distributed resources — home batteries, thermostats, backup generators, flexible industrial load — operated together so the grid sees them as one dispatchable resource. It sells the same products a power station sells without any single plant existing.

A financial power purchase agreement: the buyer pays the project a fixed price and receives the market price plus the renewable certificates, without ever taking the electricity. Corporates far from the project — Verizon, Microsoft — use it to claim clean energy.

A control mode that makes a grid-forming inverter behave like a traditional spinning generator, resisting frequency change as though it had rotating mass it does not have. It is how an inverter-based plant supplies the stabilizing behavior retiring thermal plants used to provide for free, and it is what makes black start and off-grid running possible.

Holding a converter's output voltage steady as its input voltage and its load change. A regulated converter watches its output and corrects continuously; an unregulated one simply follows its input by a fixed ratio, trading precision for efficiency and relying on regulation elsewhere in the chain.

A partial or near-total collapse of supply voltage lasting a few cycles while protection clears a fault somewhere on the network. Sags are far more common than outages and cause most unplanned industrial disruption — and the damage usually comes from equipment disconnecting in response rather than from the sag itself.

The modern HVDC converter type, built from transistors that switch off on command. It controls real and reactive power independently, can feed a weak or dead network, and is built as a stack of small identical submodules.

The share of votes someone controls in a company, which can differ sharply from the share of the economics they own when there are multiple share classes. Control normally follows votes, and consolidation in the accounts follows control.

Valve-regulated lead-acid: the sealed lead-acid battery that backed data-center UPS for decades — cheap per kilowatt for a few minutes of runtime, but heavy, sensitive to heat, good for only a few hundred deep cycles and replaced every few years. Lithium-ion has been displacing it in new UPS installations on life and footprint.

Voltage regulator module: the last conversion stage on the server board, stepping the rack's supply down to roughly one volt at the processor die. It is the final link in a chain of conversions running from the transmission line to the chip, and every one of them costs efficiency.

The thin disc of silicon on which chips are made, hundreds at a time, before being cut apart. The share of those that work is the yield, and because a wafer costs the same whether its chips work or not, yield is what turns a manufacturing process into a price.

The size of the disc a chip fab processes at once. A larger wafer carries proportionally more die for roughly the same handling cost per wafer, so moving from 150 mm to 200 mm is one of the few ways to cut the cost of a power device without changing the device.
Weighted average lease term: the rent-weighted number of years remaining across a landlord's leases. Longer is safer for a lender or a sponsor because the rent is locked for longer.

A large revolving loan that funds several projects through construction at once, each one leaving the warehouse when it is refinanced at commercial operation. It is how a private developer builds a portfolio without raising a separate loan for every site.

An undertaking by a third party to pay if a supplier fails to honour its warranty obligations, up to a stated amount. Being capped and time-limited, it covers a bad year rather than a bad decade, and it does not replace a supplier that is still present and competent late in an asset's life.

Money a supplier provisions when a sale is booked, against the future cost of the guarantees it just gave. Sizing it honestly needs a degradation model good enough to forecast capacity top-ups and a defect-rate assumption good enough to forecast field failures — which is why aggressive terms from a thinly reserved supplier are a warning rather than a bargain.

The mass of water relative to cement in a concrete mix, and the single strongest determinant of its strength and durability. Adding water at the truck to make placement easier trades permanent strength for temporary convenience.

Spraying water or steam into a gas turbine, which adds mass flow and so raises output, while absorbing heat and suppressing nitrogen-oxide formation at the same time. It buys megawatts and emissions margin with water — a hard trade in the arid places where hot-day output loss is worst.

A commitment to restore as much water to the relevant watershed as a facility withdraws, usually by funding conservation or forest-health projects. Distinct from a low water usage effectiveness, which measures what the cooling system consumes.
Treating used water to a standard fit for reuse rather than discharging it. A campus that promises to return or reuse its water has to build and operate a plant to do it.

A day on which weather prevents work, allowed for in the programme in advance so that ordinary seasonal conditions are the contractor's risk and only abnormal weather is an excusable event. The allowance is why a slipped start can cost far more than its own length — pushing exposed work across a seasonal boundary loses the whole season, not the days.
The lowest temperature air can be cooled to by evaporating water into it. It is always at or below the dry-bulb temperature, and it is the floor an evaporative device works against.

Every material the coolant touches — plate metal, pipe, hose lining, seals, cold-plate copper. They must be compatible with each other and with the fluid's inhibitor package, because a single mismatched metal or elastomer in the loop is where corrosion, leaching or leaks begin.

The floor area of a data hall where racks actually stand, as distinct from the plant rooms, switchrooms and battery rooms that serve it. It is what gets leased, so every square metre spent on plant is measured against it.

A broker that does not deal with the insured directly but places business the retail broker cannot reach — surplus-lines markets, specialist underwriters, London. It adds a second commission to the chain, which is the price of access to capacity the retail broker has no appointment with.

The tariff a Texas wire company charges a generator or battery connected to its distribution system rather than to the transmission grid. It carries demand charges that storage owners argue penalise a resource that reduces peak load.

A semiconductor whose electrons need much more energy to jump into conduction than silicon's do. The wider gap lets the material hold off a high voltage across a much thinner layer, which is why silicon carbide and gallium nitride switch faster and waste less than silicon at the same rating.

A utility's exposure to damages when its equipment starts a wildfire — the largest tail risk in the western US since the California fires, and the reason mitigation plans, public-safety shutoffs and liability legislation now sit in rate cases. Where a state caps or funds the liability the utility's cost of capital falls; where it does not, every dry, windy day is a balance-sheet event.

The commission-reviewed program a utility runs to keep its lines from starting fires and to limit the damage if they do: undergrounding and covered conductor in high-risk zones, faster-acting protection settings, vegetation clearance, weather stations and cameras, and the rules for shutting off power in dangerous wind. Its cost is recovered through a rider and its adequacy is argued in the liability case after the fire.

How much fault current a piece of equipment can survive, as opposed to interrupt — the bus bars, supports and enclosure must hold together for the cycles it takes an upstream device to clear. Magnetic force between conductors goes with current squared, so bracing a bus for a higher fault level is a physical redesign, not a paperwork change.

A certification arrangement in which the manufacturer's own laboratory runs the tests while the certification body's engineer witnesses them, so the results count toward certification without shipping samples to the certifier's lab. Used with large Asian cell and system makers.

A gas's heating value divided by the square root of its relative density, which predicts how much heat it will deliver through a given burner at a given pressure. Two gases with the same value are interchangeable without re-tuning, so a machine's declared Wobbe band is the real measure of how much fuel variation it can absorb.

A cell whose electrodes and separator are wound into a continuous roll before being placed in its housing. It is fast to manufacture and long established, but it fills a large rectangular can less evenly than a stack, which is one reason very large storage formats have moved toward stacked construction.

Water usage effectiveness: water consumed per unit of IT energy, the cooling counterpart to PUE. Closed-loop and air-cooled designs spend a little more electricity to spend almost no water, which in a water-stressed watershed is usually the more permittable trade.

Xenon-135, a fission product with an enormous appetite for thermal neutrons, builds up after a power reduction and suppresses the chain reaction for hours. It is the physical reason a thermal reactor is a poor load-follower.

The stabilised net operating income a development is expected to produce, divided by everything it cost to build. Compared against the cap rate on a finished building, it says whether construction created value.

A listed company that owns operating power plants under long-term contracts and passes most of the cash they generate to shareholders as a dividend. It buys finished assets rather than developing them, usually from a sponsor that keeps the development business private.

The instant an alternating waveform passes through zero volts, twice per cycle. For a fraction of a millisecond nothing sustains an arc, so an arc drawn on AC tends to extinguish itself — and almost every protective device in an AC building quietly relies on that. Direct current never offers the instant, which is why DC protection has to be engineered rather than inherited.
